Repeating the same action while expecting different results is the very definition of "insanity."

It seems that is also the message the Republicans are trying to convey to voters in this midterm election.

And they mean it literally.

Political analysts say current data suggests a "blue wave" could hand the Democrats back control of the House, driven in part by Donald Trump's approval ratings hitting record lows.

The Republicans are losing ground in House races unless they can find a message that persuades voters to stick with them.

House Speaker Mike Johnson had a chance to make that case to voters during an interview on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Tuesday — and instead handed Democrats a gift.

"We're going to do exactly what we've done over the last two years," Johnson said, "and that is create the conditions for a strong America."

He went on to elaborate:

Johnson's pitch — promising to stay the course on policies that have inflamed tensions with Iran, sent gas prices climbing and fueled inflation — predictably fell flat.

In fact, the moment played out much like Vice President JD Vance's desperate plea earlier this month for voters to "give us another chance," which also fell completely flat.
